newsitem.title: USA: Ford concerned by surge in Japan car exports.
newsitem.headline: Ford concerned by surge in Japan car exports.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Vice Chairman Wayne Booker said on Tuesday that the company was concerned about the recent increase in Japanese auto exports to the United States.

"Japanese auto exports to the U.S. have increased substantially over the last six months, and that is an area of concern to us as American automotive producers," Booker told reporters at a U.S.-Japan business conference in San Francisco.
He said the Japanese market share in the United States had "grown about four points over the last several months."
"And therefore, of course, that is a trend that we would not like to see continue," he said.
Booker could not say exactly how much the increase in exports was directly related to the recent weakening of the yen. "But there has to be some relationship," he said.
